maker: Trossen Robotics (ALOHA: T. Z. Zhao et al.)
name: ALOHA leader arm (WidowX-250 6DOF)

sources.title: T. Z. Zhao, V. Kumar, S. Levine, C. Finn, Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware, arXiv:2304.13705 (HTML version)
sources.covers: joint-space mapping from the WidowX leader to the ViperX follower, the 50 Hz teleoperation, the handle-and-scissor mechanism

sources.title: Interbotix X-Series Arms documentation, WidowX-250 6DOF specifications (Trossen Robotics)
sources.covers: degrees of freedom, reach, repeatability, accuracy, servos

sources.title: ALOHA documentation 2.0, Specifications (Trossen Robotics)
sources.covers: the leader arms "WidowX 250 S - Aloha Version", the followers "ViperX 300 S - Aloha Version"

note: ALOHA teleoperates "by backdriving the smaller WidowX ('the leader'), whose joints are synchronized with the larger ViperX ('the follower')": "direct joint-space mapping"; the two arms "are approximately scaled versions of each other" (same_joints false: the WidowX's ranges are not the ViperX's, and DexVantage takes the follower's ranges, an assumption the device record says). "Both the teleoperation and data recording happen at 50Hz" (tracking_hz 50). A 3D-printed "handle and scissor" mechanism gives continuous gripper control. WidowX-250 6DOF (Trossen): "Degrees of Freedom 6", "Reach 650mm", "Repeatability 1mm", "Accuracy 5 - 8mm" (accuracy_mm 8, the upper end; the arm's own positioning accuracy, not a teleop figure), servos DYNAMIXEL XM430-W350 and XL430-W250 with "4096 positions". Not stated: the leader's mass, latency.

tracking_hz.quote: "Both the teleoperation and data recording happen at 50Hz."

workspace.quote: The workspace is the follower's own (joint to joint); the source states no separate volume.

feedback.quote: Not stated (the leader is backdriven; no force feedback is described).
